_about: Chord shapes. 'checkShared' = strings that share all their overtones with another string but which the synthetic tests show can still be checked. 'frets' lists strings from 6 (low E, thickest) to 1 (high E, thinnest). null = don't play that string (X), 0 = open string. 'fingers' uses 1 index, 2 middle, 3 ring, 4 little (null = no finger). 'steps' is the order to place fingers in build-the-chord mode.

chords.name: E minor

steps.text: Middle finger, 2nd fret, 5th string (A). Press with the very tip, just behind the fret wire.
Ring finger, 2nd fret, 4th string (D), right next to your middle finger.
Strum all six strings. Every string should ring.

chords.notes: One of the easiest chords on the guitar. All six strings ring.

chords.name: A minor

steps.text: Index finger, 1st fret, 2nd string (B). Curl it so it doesn't touch the 1st string.
Ring finger, 2nd fret, 3rd string (G), just below your middle finger.
Strum from the 5th string (A) down. Don't play the 6th string.

chords.notes: Same shape as E major, moved across one string.

chords.name: A major

steps.text: Ring finger, 2nd fret, 2nd string (B). Three fingers in a row; they won't all fit right behind the fret, so angle them slightly.
Strum from the 5th string (A) down. Check the 1st string still rings.

chords.notes: Three fingers squeezed into one fret. The 1st string is the one that usually gets muted.

chords.name: D major

steps.text: Ring finger, 3rd fret, 2nd string (B). The fingers make a small triangle.
Strum only the top four strings, starting from the 4th string (D).

chords.notes: Only four strings. Aim your strum at the 4th string.

chords.name: G major

steps.text: Strum all six strings. The three middle strings ring open.

chords.notes: A wide stretch. The open 4th, 3rd and 2nd strings must not be touched.
